w: The opening ceremony of the 1984 Winter Olympics played out here, on what is still Bosnia and Herzegovina's largest stadium. Locals call it Asim Ferhatović Hase, home turf of FK Sarajevo and occasional host to the national football team -- Olympic history hiding inside a football ground's name.
_facts: Hosted the opening ceremony of the 1984 Winter Olympics
Largest stadium in Bosnia and Herzegovina
Also known as Stadium Asim Ferhatović Hase, home of FK Sarajevo

w: A single stone arch spans the Miljacka east of Sarajevo's old town, carrying the puzzling name of Kozija ćuprija -- the Goat's Bridge. Set in the Babića Bašća neighbourhood of Stari Grad, it's registered as a protected architectural heritage monument: a modest river crossing nobody has fully explained.
s: A stone river crossing nobody's explained
_facts: Large stone bridge crossing the Miljacka river east of Sarajevo's downtown
Located in the Babića Bašća neighbourhood, Municipality of Stari Grad
Registered as a heritage site / architectural heritage monument
